name: Nosferatu crypt-lid quick-return
summary: A crank and slotted lever ease a coffin lid open over two-thirds of a turn and slam it in the last third, while a cam on the crank sits the vampire up.

ratio.typical: lid swing 73.7°; open-to-slam time ratio 2.39:1; the occupant rises 72°

topology.notes: ground, crank, slotted lever with the lid, rocker, link and occupant (the hip arm with the figurine on it), with the cam keyed on the crank shaft and the cam roller turning on its stud in the rocker; the crank pin's track roller runs in the lever's slot (pin-in-slot) and the cam roller on the cam (cam contact). The mobility counted from kin is 3: the cam is a body of its own keyed on the crank shaft, and the cam roller's spin on its stud is a passive freedom; the true mobility is 1.

explain.motion: A crank turning steadily about C carries a roller in a slot cut along the lid lever, which pivots at O above it. The lever rocks between two extremes, reached when the crank is square to the slot. Because the crank pin is far from O while it travels the long way round and close to O on the short way, the lever swings slowly one way and fast the other. The lid is fixed to the lever, so it rises 73.7° over 253.7° of crank and falls over 106.3°, a time ratio of 2.39:1. A cam on the crank shaft swings a rocker, and a link carries the swing to the occupant's hip shaft: he sits up 72° while the lid is high, holds, and is lying down again as the slam begins.
explain.forces: Drive torque reaches the lever as a roller force square to the slot, so the lever sees the most force per unit torque on the slam stroke, when the roller is only 20 mm from O. The lid's own weight assists the slam; on the opening stroke the crank lifts it through the long lever arm, so the motor works hardest just after the lid leaves the frame. The cam lifts the occupant with its pressure angle under 22° and lets him down under his own weight.
explain.benefits: One continuously running motor produces the full theatrical sequence: a slow, suspenseful opening, a moment of hesitation at full height, and a fast close. No controller, limit switch or second motor is involved, and the timing never drifts.
explain.limits: There is no true dwell; the lid lingers within 2° of fully open for only 35° of crank, so any occupant must sit up promptly. The slam reverses the roller's load in the slot at speed, which wears the slot flanks first; the Commercial build adds a polymer slot liner rather than relying on the patron's screams to mask the noise.

build.ground: the coffin on its turned legs, the base, the side frame and the hip bracket; the lid hinge O level with the coffin's rim beyond its head end, the crank centre C 50 mm below it, the rocker pivot G and the hip shaft H
build.defining_relations: Lever extremes where the crank is square to the slot: cos β = r/d, β = 53.13° with r = 30 and d = 50. Slam stroke 2β = 106.3° of crank, opening stroke 360° − 2β = 253.7°, time ratio 2.39:1. Lever swing 2 asin(r/d) = 73.74°. Peak lever speed per unit crank speed r/(d − r) = 1.5 on the slam, r/(d + r) = 0.375 on the opening, a factor of 4. Cam, in crank degrees from shut: cycloidal rise from 140° to 212°, dwell to 240°, cycloidal return by 262°. The roller centre stands at the pitch radius rb + s from C (base circle 28 mm, roller 5 mm, lift 12.7 mm) on the arc of the rocker's 32 mm arm about G, so the rocker turns where the two circles meet; the cam's outline is the roller's envelope on that path. The four-bar G, E, F, H (rocker output arm 52 mm at 150° to the roller arm, link 35.4 mm, hip arm 16 mm) turns the swing into 72° at the hip, its transmission angle never under 61°.
build.notes: The input counts from 159° of crank past shut, so the drawing opens with the lid high and the occupant up; the lid and occupant angles read from shut and from lying. Range: crank 360° continuous; lid from 0° (shut) to 73.7° open; occupant from 0° (lying) to 72° (up), fully up from 212° to 240° of crank and lying again by 262°. Lever angle = atan2(−d + r sin θ, r cos θ); lid open = −53.13° − lever angle. The crank turns the way that puts the long arc on the opening. The roller is nearest O at mid-slam, so the slot reaches 14 mm from O. The cam and rocker differ from the first concept's (base 14 mm, lift 18.3 mm, arms 28 and 38 mm): that cam's pressure angle reached 69° on the rise and its outline undercut the roller; a 28 mm base circle and longer arms keep it under 22° with no undercut, and keep the cam's lobe clear of the rocker's axle. The hip shaft stands 106 mm from the hinge, 6 mm further than the concept's, so the occupant's collar clears the open lid by 18.5 mm, not 13. The drive sits close against the drive-side wall on a side frame: the lid hinge's and the rocker's axles stand in it and the crank shaft runs in a housing on its coffin side, with the motor beyond the head end; the hip arm turns on an axle in a small bracket outboard, hung on two standoffs from the side frame, and a tube on it carries the figure through the side frame and the coffin wall.

review.note: T2 review 2026-10-28, six phases drawn from the solved motion at 0, 60, 120, 180, 240 and 300 degrees of crank in VIEW 300 24: tweak. The principle is the crank and slotted lever: the lever's two extremes are the lines from O tangent to the crank circle (the crank square to the slot), drawn as construction lines with the slow opening arc (253.7 degrees) and the quick slam arc (106.3 degrees) of the crank pin between them; the lid tip carries the comet and 15 degree ticks, spread out on the opening and bunched on the slam. The cam, rocker and four-bar that sit the occupant up are second: a detail view of the cam and its roller, and the crown's trace. Changes from the catalogue entry: the cam and rocker were redesigned (base 28 mm, lift 12.7 mm, roller arm 32 mm, output arm 52 mm at 150 degrees, link 35.4 mm, hip arm 16 mm, the hip shaft at 106 mm) because the concept's cam reached a 69 degree pressure angle on the rise and undercut its roller; the timing, the 72 degree rise and the pivots G and H stay. The occupant clears the lid by 18.5 mm (13 in the concept). Default view from the foot end, the drive on the right, so the occupant faces the viewer as he sits up. Solve checks: swing 73.74, time ratio 2.388, rise 72, lingering 35 degrees, pin radius 20 mm, pressure angle 21.2 on the rise.

examples.detail: The standard lid drive for coffins, crypt doors and sarcophagi, where a 20 rpm gearmotor gives a 2.1 s open and a 0.9 s slam, a rhythm scare designers call "the long breath in".
The same quick-return snaps hinged lids on seasonal chocolate boxes, giving the operator time to place the tray on the slow stroke.
Motorised trick-or-treat bowls, where the lid stays near closed for most of the cycle and the quick-return gives children a fair but brief window.
Trapdoor and casket effects, run quietly on the slow stroke and allowed to bang on the fast one because the orchestra covers it.
